name: empty
description: A placeholder displayed when a list, panel, or section has no content. Icon + title + description + optional action buttons. Three Variants control container surface. Purely presentational — no Radix primitive.

intent.Default: No fill, no stroke, no radius — transparent. Use inside cards, sheets, dialogs that already provide the surface.
intent.Outline: No fill, color/border/default stroke, radius/lg. Use for bordered empty areas — list zones, table bodies, dropzone areas.
intent.Background: color/background/subtle fill, no stroke, radius/lg. Use for page-level or sidebar empty states with no other framing.

media.fillNote: In Background variant, media steps up to color/surface/default to stay distinct from the subtle fill behind it.

composition.structure: V AUTO-LAYOUT, CENTER×CENTER: header (media 36×36 + title + description) → content (btn-primary + btn-outline, H AUTO-LAYOUT)
composition.iconCustomisation: Replace the default folder icon with a context-specific icon: file, search, inbox, calendar, bell, users, bar-chart.

buttonVisibility.readOnly: no buttons — or a text link to request access

behavior.architecture: Purely presentational — no Radix primitive, no built-in state. Conditionally rendered by the parent when data is absent.
behavior.renderTiming: Render only after data load completes with zero results. Show skeleton or spinner during loading.

accessibility.role: No implicit role — renders as <div>. Add role='status' when empty state appears dynamically after search or filter.
accessibility.icon: aria-hidden='true' on icon — title and description carry the message.
accessibility.titleRequirement: title must be descriptive enough to stand alone as the accessible label.
accessibility.descriptionRequirement: description provides context and the next step — not a restatement of the title.

constraints: Variant=Default inside containers that already provide a surface (cards, sheets, dialogs).
Variant=Outline for bordered empty areas (table bodies, list panels, dropzones).
Variant=Background for page-level or sidebar empty states with no other framing.
Do not use Variant=Background inside a card — the card already provides the surface; a subtle fill inside it creates unintended double-layering.
Do not show the empty state during loading — show skeleton/spinner first.
Replace the default folder icon with one contextually relevant to the empty state.
Keep description to one or two short sentences.
Do not override button fills from within the empty component.

useCases: A project list that has no projects yet — first-use onboarding state with a 'Create Project' CTA
A search results panel that returns zero matches — with a 'Clear filters' or 'Try different keywords' action
An inbox or notification feed that has been fully read or cleared ('You're all caught up.')
A team members table where no members have been invited yet ('Invite your team to get started.')
A calendar or event list with no upcoming events ('No events scheduled — add one to get started.')
A filtered data table that returns nothing after applying active filters

Default.whenToUse: Empty state lives inside a container that already provides a surface

Outline.whenToUse: Empty state needs its own clear boundary in an open layout

Background.whenToUse: Empty state is the primary content of a page section with no other framing

comparedTo.situation: Data is still loading and content is expected to appear
comparedTo.notInstead: empty (showing empty state during a load is a false negative — the data hasn't arrived yet)

comparedTo.situation: Something went wrong and the page has content but an error occurred
comparedTo.notInstead: empty (alert communicates failure; empty communicates absence)

comparedTo.situation: The list has items but the user needs to be prompted to add more
comparedTo.notInstead: empty (empty state is for zero-item states, not low-count nudges)

notes: empty is a custom design system component — implementation is a custom React component, not a shadcn base.

darkMode.notes: No known dark mode differences — all tokens are semantic and mode-aware.
